title: Armstrong's loyalty to New Orleans and a later jam at the Royal Orleans
summary: Their first talk, Louis's pride in New Orleans musicians, and a later jam with Paul Barbarin when Louis visited.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: So, uh, when you met him that night, uh, back in 1930, did you all spend a long time talking?

Yeah, we talked. We had different things we talked about, and he was very proud to see, you know, some of his eyes. Mm-hmm. Trying to keep music alive, and going to play. Mm-hmm. He was always proud of New Orleans musicians. There was nothing. You know, you know, plenty of people went up and told you they were from New Orleans. I remember it came from, uh, Baton Rouge or something. He'd say, man, I'm from New Orleans. You know, everybody was from New Orleans, indeed. Yeah. And Louie would say, man, uh, I'm a New Orleans man or something like that. Yeah. He had a good voice, but he really was dedicated to New Orleans. Louie loved everyone. He loved people, but he would never, anybody would say, I'm from New Orleans, that was it. Yeah. He was a very loyal man.
Very, very, very fireman. And, uh, that's where Louie was.
